title: “Monks, I do not see any other class of things that is as diverse as the mind. Those beings in the animal realm — such…
content: “Monks, I do not see any other class of things that is as diverse as the mind. Those beings in the animal realm — such beings are diverse because of their minds. Therefore, monks, one should constantly reflect on one’s own mind thus: ‘For a long time, this mind has been defiled by greed, hatred, and delusion. Through the defilement of the mind, beings are defiled. Through the purification of the mind, beings are purified.’”

title: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing.…
content: “Monks, there are these five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? Forms cognizable by the eye—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. Sounds cognizable by the ear … Odors cognizable by the nose … Tastes cognizable by the tongue … Tangibles cognizable by the body—these are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. These, monks, are the five strands of sensual pleasure.”

title: Though warned by the divine messengers, Young men remain heedless, They sorrow for a long time, Born in a low state. But the true person…
content:
Though warned by the divine messengers,
Young men remain heedless,
They sorrow for a long time,
Born in a low state.
But the true person here,
Warned by the divine messengers,
Is never heedless
In the noble Dhamma.
Seeing fear in clinging,
In birth and death,
Released from clinging,
Birth and death are ended.
Attaining security and bliss,
Here and now fully extinguished,
All enmity and fear —
They have overcome all.
All pain and sorrow —
All are transcended.

title: “‘Come, monk, guard the sense faculties. When you see a form with the eye, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular…
content: “‘Come, monk, guard the sense faculties. When you see a form with the eye, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the eye, practice restraint of the eye. When you hear a sound with the ear … smell an odor with the nose … taste a flavor with the tongue … feel a touch with the body … cognize a phenomenon with the mind, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the mind faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the mind, practice restraint of the mind.’”

title: “Pleasant and delightful are sensual pleasures, In various forms both coarse and refined — Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure, Wander alone like…
content:
“Pleasant and delightful are sensual pleasures,
In various forms both coarse and refined —
Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure,
Wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”

“This is a boil, this is a calamity,
This is a disease, this is a dart —
Seeing the danger in these strands of pleasure,
Wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”

title: Elder Nun Mother of Abhayā: From the soles of the feet upward, From the top of the head downward — Contemplate this body — This…
content:
Elder Nun Mother of Abhayā:

From the soles of the feet upward,
From the top of the head downward —
Contemplate this body —
This body is truly impure,
Truly foul, stinking.

Thus abiding,
All sensual desire is uprooted.
Fever is abandoned —
I am cooled, at peace.

title: “Monks, form is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not…
content: “Monks, form is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Feeling … Perception … Formations … Consciousness is suffering. What is suffering is not-self. What is not-self should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom: ‘This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.’ Seeing thus, monks, a well-taught noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form … disenchanted with feeling … disenchanted with perception … disenchanted with formations … disenchanted with consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, he is liberated … ‘… there is no more of this state of being.’”

title: “Here, venerable sir, many people in Sāvatthi are mostly intoxicated with sensual pleasures, living as if drunk, attached, lustful, infatuated, bound, and bewitched by sensual…
content:
“Here, venerable sir, many people in Sāvatthi are mostly intoxicated with sensual pleasures, living as if drunk, attached, lustful, infatuated, bound, and bewitched by sensual pleasures.” The Blessed One, understanding the meaning, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

Beings are attached
To various sensual pleasures,
They see no fault
In the defilements that fetter.

Indeed, beings bound by fetters,
Do not cross over
This great, broad flood.

title: “Knowing this body to be like a clay pot, Fortifying this mind like a city, Fight Māra with the sword of wisdom, Guard your conquest,…
content:
“Knowing this body to be like a clay pot,
Fortifying this mind like a city,
Fight Māra with the sword of wisdom,
Guard your conquest, and be free of attachment.”

“Before long, alas, this body
Will lie on the ground,
Cast aside, devoid of consciousness,
Like a useless log.”

title: Standing to one side, the deity Tayana recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One: O brahmin, striving, cut the stream, Abandon and…
content:
Standing to one side, the deity Tayana recited this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:

O brahmin, striving, cut the stream,
Abandon and destroy
All clinging to sensual desires.
Without cutting sensual desires,
A sage cannot attain unification of mind.
If you do what should be done,
Be steadfast and energetic.
If a goer-forth is lazy,
He scatters even more dust.
Not doing is better than doing badly —
Doing badly leads to suffering afterward.
Having done, do it well —
Doing well brings no suffering.
Like holding grass the wrong way,
It can cut your hand,
So too, the ascetic life wrongly practiced
Drags one to hell.
Any lazy conduct,
Any defiled practice,
Any evil action in the holy life
Does not yield great fruit.
